steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Every evening as the horizon melted from gold to velvety purple, Rowan Hale climbed the spiral stairs of Mariner’s Reach Lighthouse with a brass lamp in one hand and a tin mug of tea in the other. The lamp had belonged to his father, and the mug was chipped from years of salty air, but both felt like anchors in the restless sea of memory.

Rowan’s world was measured in flashes: one long beam sweeping across black water every twelve seconds. He spoke to the gulls, mended nets for the fishermen who rarely came ashore, and kept meticulous logs that no one read. Yet he never felt alone. Beneath the lighthouse floorboards, waves hummed ancient lullabies, and sometimes—on nights when a storm bruised the sky—he heard a faint knock, as though the ocean itself was asking to be let in.

One winter night a squall roared in without warning. Rain lashed the glass, drowning out even the lighthouse’s rhythmic heartbeat. Through the driving sheets Rowan caught sight of a tiny sloop, tossed like a toy in a child’s bath. He cranked the lantern higher, widening the circle of light, and wrapped a crimson flag around his lantern to burn a warning red across the tempest. Hours passed. The lighthouse shuddered, but Rowan’s arm never wavered.

At dawn the sea lay calm as spilled mercury, and driftwood cluttered the rocky shore. There, half-buried in seaweed, Rowan found a single message bottle: “To whoever stands watch—your light saved us. We’ll return when the sun shines.” No name, no signature, just gratitude pressed between glass and saltwater tears.

Days turned into seasons. Visitors came and went, but the sloop never returned. Still Rowan Hale kept watch, night after night, guided by the promise of unseen lives depending on a circle of light. And so the lighthouse keeper’s legacy shone unseen across the moving deep, illuminating both the living waters before him and the quiet, endless horizon within his own steadfast heart.
